clues.clue: Cylindrical bollards when viewed from the front — a shape not shared with other Nordic countries.
Solid white side lines (when present) and a center line that can be white or yellow, sometimes with a secondary stripe.
Minor directional signs have white text on blue background with a bold arrow on the sides. Warning signs are triangular with red border and yellow background.
Finnish uses special characters ä and ö. Often has double vowels and long words. Street names end in '-katu' or '-ntie'.
Flat terrain with dense forests. Dirt and gravel roads are common, especially in rural areas.
Drives on the right.
Standard wooden or concrete poles without distinctive national features.
Black-and-white bollards, often with a grey reflector. Near intersections, reflectors can be orange. Come in various shapes: wedge, round, or thin and curved.
White dashed side lines with a white center line. The gaps between side dashes are notably longer than the dashes themselves.
Directional signs are blue with white text and a thin arrow on the sides. Chevrons use distinctive yellow and blue colors.

Drives on the right.

Norwegian uses special characters å, æ, and ø. Street names end in '-vei'/'-veien' or '-gate'/'-gata'.

Drives on the right.
